test_title: PYST 47: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 03 Sept, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Which of the following courts is known as the 'Guardian of the Constitution' in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Supreme Court**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Supreme Court of India is known as the **'Guardian of the Constitution'** because it ensures the enforcement and protection of the fundamental rights of citizens.
 
• It has the authority to interpret the Constitution and resolve disputes between the Union and States or among States themselves.
 
• Under Article 32 of the Indian Constitution, the Supreme Court guarantees the right to constitutional remedies, allowing individuals to approach the court directly in case of violation of their fundamental rights.
 
• The Supreme Court is vested with the power of judicial review, which enables it to strike down any law or executive action that it deems unconstitutional.
 
• It is the apex judicial authority in India, and its decisions are binding on all other courts in the country.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **District Court**

 
 
• District Courts are subordinate courts that deal with civil and criminal cases at the district level.
 
• They function under the supervision of the High Court of the respective state.
 
• While they play an important role in the justice delivery system, they do not have constitutional authority like the Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• **High Court**
 
 
• High Courts are the highest judicial bodies at the state level and handle civil, criminal, and constitutional matters within their jurisdiction.
 
• They also have the power of judicial review but are subordinate to the Supreme Court.
 
• High Courts can interpret the Constitution but cannot act as the ultimate guardian of constitutional provisions like the Supreme Court.
 
 
 
• **Lok Adalat**
 
 
• Lok Adalat is a system of alternative dispute resolution in India aimed at resolving disputes outside the formal judicial process.
 
• It is governed by the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, and is primarily used for settling civil disputes and minor criminal cases.
 
• While it promotes speedy and amicable settlements, it does not have constitutional authority or the power to interpret the Constitution.
